reason: E1 directly supports the core premise that Cr, Ni, and Mn nanocluster at GBs and reduce cohesion, causing ductility loss in the quinary alloy. However, E2 concerns a different alloy (Fe40Mn40Cr10Co10) and a different mechanism (mechanically derived short-range order at 77 K), providing no evidence for the claim that removing elements alters segregation-driven clustering in the equiatomic subsets. The hypothesis therefore relies on a single piece of evidence for the quinary baseline, with no cited support for the predicted behavior of the quaternary and ternary alloys.
premises: Nanoclustering of Cr, Ni, and Mn at grain boundaries reduces GB cohesion in CrMnFeCoNi
This nanoclustering promotes crack initiation along GBs during deformation at intermediate temperatures
Removing key elements (Cr, Mn, Ni) in quaternary/ternary subsets will alter or reduce this segregation-driven clustering
Reduced nanoclustering will improve GB cohesion and delay crack initiation
The effect is element-specific, not merely dependent on the number of constituents
